Jonas / Team —

We triaged the traces Elena sent. Quick notes from the infra side:
- Kernel selector change was rolled at 02:30 PT as part of the servicing optimizer push (selector v3.4 -> v3.5).
- Observed increased collisions for KV-cache entries for redwood-v2-q4_k on GPU hosts that are dominantly shared by hosted-api traffic. KV cache fragmentation is causing more cache re-population and higher compute on first token, which suppresses sustained tokens/sec.
- Continuous batching latency buckets widened; batch sizes are lower but CPU/GPU occupancy is uneven on the new kernel path.

Immediate mitigation options (with pros/cons):
1) Canary rollback of kernel-selector to v3.4 for the affected pool (fast, should recover TPS; risk: misses other optimizer improvements).
2) Route SpeedBuy traffic to reserved/dedicated pool for 12–24h (safer; may increase their cost; needs capacity check).
3) Param tweak: reduce aggressive KV eviction on the q4_k path and increase prefix caching window (medium work, may mitigate without rollback).

We recommend option 1 now for fastest restoration while we run parameter tuning in parallel. Initiating rollback will be done in stages (canary -> 30% -> all) with monitoring.

Attaching a Grafana snapshot (grafana-snapshot-p99-20280418.png) showing the p95/p99 trend and a short perf diff.

—Laura
SR Manager, Serving Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quick update from the on-call runbook: we started a canary rollback of the kernel-selector at 13:10 PT (canary on 10% of affected pool). Observed: p95 returned to baseline within ~8 minutes on canary hosts; tokens/sec on canary hosts returned to expected levels. Next actions:
- Continue staged rollback (10% -> 30% at 14:30 -> 100% overnight).
- While rolling back, infra will increase prefix caching window for q4_k and run a background rewarm job to refill KV caches.
- CS will draft a customer note and propose 10% service credit for the affected 4-hour window (TBD with Finance/Legal).
